{
  "id": "p_000",
  "summary": "A minimal REST API for task management supporting CRUD operations with endpoints for creating, reading (single and list), updating, and deleting tasks, using standard HTTP methods and JSON payloads.",
  "approach": "Adopt a resource-oriented design with '/tasks' as the base path for collection operations and '/tasks/{id}' for individual tasks. Use GET for reading, POST for creating, PUT for updating, and DELETE for deleting tasks. Define JSON structures for request and response bodies based on the task schema (id, title, description, status, created_at, updated_at), and implement consistent error responses with {\"error\": \"message\"}.",
  "tradeoffs": [
    "No authentication or authorization, making it unsuitable for production without additional security layers.",
    "Lack of pagination or filtering, which may lead to performance issues with large numbers of tasks.",
    "No versioning mechanism, increasing the risk of breaking changes in future API evolution."
  ],
  "evidence": [
    "REST principles advocate for stateless communication, uniform interface, and resource-based URLs (Fielding, 2000).",
    "Standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) are semantically appropriate for CRUD operations, as per HTTP/1.1 specifications.",
    "JSON is a widely adopted data interchange format for APIs, ensuring simplicity and ease of use."
  ],

}
